For a pure state write $\psi=\sqrt{\mathcal P}\,e^{iS/x}$. Then
\[
\partial_\mu\ln\psi=\frac12\partial_\mu\ln\mathcal P+\frac{i}{x}\partial_\mu S
=\frac{m}{x}\bigl(u_\mu+i\pi_\mu\bigr),
\]
using the Madelung–Bohm velocities $u_\mu=\frac{x}{2m}\partial_\mu\ln\mathcal P$ and $\pi_\mu=\frac1m\partial_\mu S$.

The Fubini–Study metric for pure states is
\[
g^{\mathrm{FS}}_{\mu\nu}
=\operatorname{Re}\!\left[\langle\partial_\mu\psi|\partial_\nu\psi\rangle
-\langle\partial_\mu\psi|\psi\rangle\langle\psi|\partial_\nu\psi\rangle\right].
\]

Substituting the expression above and using $\int \mathcal P\,\partial_\mu\ln\mathcal P=0$ (so $\langle u_\mu\rangle=0$) gives
\[
g^{\mathrm{FS}}_{\mu\nu}
=\frac{m^{2}}{x^{2}}\Bigl[\langle u_\mu u_\nu\rangle
+\langle\pi_\mu\pi_\nu\rangle-\langle\pi_\mu\rangle\langle\pi_\nu\rangle\Bigr]_{\mathcal P}
=\frac{m^{2}}{x^{2}}\Bigl[\operatorname{Cov}(u_\mu,u_\nu)
+\operatorname{Cov}(\pi_\mu,\pi_\nu)\Bigr]_{\mathcal P}.
\]

Hence the proportionality factor is $C=m^{2}/x^{2}$.

Write the wavefunction in Madelung form $\psi=\sqrt{\mathcal{P}}\,e^{iS/\hbar}$. The Madelung–Bohm velocities are $\pi_\mu=\frac{1}{m}\partial_\mu S$ and $u_\mu=\frac{\hbar}{2m}\partial_\mu\ln\mathcal{P}$, so that
\[
\partial_\mu\ln\psi=\frac{1}{2}\partial_\mu\ln\mathcal{P}+\frac{i}{\hbar}\partial_\mu S
=\frac{m}{\hbar}\bigl(u_\mu+i\pi_\mu\bigr)=\frac{i m}{\hbar}\,\eta_\mu .
\]
Hence $\partial_\mu\psi=(i m/\hbar)\,\eta_\mu\psi$. The Fubini–Study (quantum Fisher) metric is
\[
g^{\mathrm{FS}}_{\mu\nu}
=\langle\partial_\mu\psi|\partial_\nu\psi\rangle-\langle\partial_\mu\psi|\psi\rangle\langle\psi|\partial_\nu\psi\rangle
=\frac{m^{2}}{\hbar^{2}}\Bigl[\langle\eta_\mu^{*}\eta_\nu\rangle-\langle\eta_\mu^{*}\rangle\langle\eta_\nu\rangle\Bigr]_{\mathcal P}.
\]
With $\eta=\pi-i u$, the real part of this complex covariance is exactly $\operatorname{Cov}(\pi_\mu,\pi_\nu)+\operatorname{Cov}(u_\mu,u_\nu)$. Therefore $C=m^{2}/\hbar^{2}=m^{2}/x^{2}$.

For a pure state written in Madelung form $\psi=\sqrt{\mathcal{P}}\,e^{iS/x}$, the Fubini–Study metric is the real part of the quantum geometric tensor:
$$g^{\mathrm{FS}}_{\mu\nu}=\operatorname{Re}\bigl[\langle\partial_\mu\psi|\partial_\nu\psi\rangle-\langle\psi|\partial_\mu\psi\rangle\langle\partial_\nu\psi|\psi\rangle\bigr].$$
Since $\partial_\mu\ln\psi=\tfrac12\partial_\mu\ln\mathcal{P}+i\,\partial_\mu S/x$, this yields
$$g^{\mathrm{FS}}_{\mu\nu}=\frac14\operatorname{Cov}_{\mathcal{P}}(\partial_\mu\ln\mathcal{P},\partial_\nu\ln\mathcal{P})+\frac1{x^2}\operatorname{Cov}_{\mathcal{P}}(\partial_\mu S,\partial_\nu S).$$
The Madelung–Bohm velocities are $\pi_\mu=\frac1m\partial_\mu S$ and $u_\mu=\frac{x}{2m}\partial_\mu\ln\mathcal{P}$, so $\partial_\mu S=m\pi_\mu$ and $\partial_\mu\ln\mathcal{P}=\frac{2m}{x}u_\mu$. Substituting gives
$$g^{\mathrm{FS}}_{\mu\nu}=\frac{m^2}{x^2}\Bigl[\operatorname{Cov}_{\mathcal{P}}(\pi_\mu,\pi_\nu)+\operatorname{Cov}_{\mathcal{P}}(u_\mu,u_\nu)\Bigr],$$
hence $C=m^2/x^2$.
